text:
If, to restrain this desire,
        mad, impossible, vain, fearful,
        and to heal myself of so dangerous an ill
        as making myself believe what I do not believe,


        it does me no good to see myself as I am,
        either too bold or too afraid,
        in such confusion that I never dare
        entrust to myself the ill I harbor,


        what good will it do me to see the picture
        of him who, falling with melted wings,
        gave his fame and name to the sea,


        and of him who weeps for his fire and folly
        among those familiar trees,
        scarcely cooled in the water?

translation.title: If, to restrain this desire
translation.editorial_note: Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
